questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am generally interested in U.S. politics and culture. I also love the east coast and New England. Thus, Boston was the ideal location.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Exceded all my expectations both academically and socially.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Information regarding the visa process and on-campus housing was minimal before arrival.
Overall though, it was possible to access the most relevant information upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance when I arrived on campus. However, I know it was available.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: More information about orientation week and social activities would have been great.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Single rooms and shared rooms in dorms or apartments.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: If you live on campus and don't have a kitchen in your room you are forced to have dining plan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Single rooms are very expensive. Dining plans are also heavily overpriced. Living in apartment style housing is much better than living in dorm-style housing. It gives you way more freedom.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: During COVID I can definitely recommend living on campus. You will have restricted access to campus and dining halls if you choose to live off-campus because of the health restrictions.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can register for most of the classes online during the registration period.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My professors and my exchange advisor were all available to answer questions about registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reach out to the professors. Most of them are very service-minded and committed to helping you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Undergraduate courses can be less challenging sometimes compared to BA courses in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All my class was seminars with a limited amount of students in each class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CAS IR378 Intelligence and Democracy 
CAS IR380 US Foreign Policy in Practice
CAS IR589 North Atlantic & European Security

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend US Foreign Policy in Practice with professor Storella and North Atlantic & European Security with professor Schilde because their teaching style is inspiring. Never had a boring class with Storolla or Schilde. They really made an effort to engage with the students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Visa application fees, Vaccination fees etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Boston is an expensive city to live in. University housing and the dining plan was definitely way more expensive than I expected. Don't by the transportation pass. Just get a T-card yourself.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many athletic and social clubs were available for exchange students from running to skiing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Join BU run club if you have the chance. Find their schedule on Facebook or Instagram. 
I met a lot of new friends through the run club (they also host great social activities).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Boston and New England. It is expensive but also worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Boston is a very European City.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs on campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging. Have been during exchange before in the U.S.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of the American culture. People really want to make new friends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Live on campus (preferably Apartment style)
2) Engage with your professors and teachers 
3) Join at least one social or athletic club.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Start saving money and applying for grants before starting your exchange semester at BU. 
Again, it is very expensive to live and study in Boston.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and learning about the most recent developments in American politics.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The visa application process during covid.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
